interest: This file provides valuable archival insight into the administrative handling of zaibatsu dissolution and anti-trust policy during the Allied occupation of Japan. It documents the dissemination of the seminal Report of the Mission on Japanese Combines (the Corwin Edwards report) to key figures connected to the Pauley Reparations Mission, highlighting inter-agency collaboration on early economic reform. Additionally, the exchange regarding FEC-230 illustrates private legal scrutiny of U.S. deconcentration policy in early 1948, coinciding precisely with the political shift toward the 'Reverse Course' when aggressive trust-busting policies were re-evaluated and ultimately curtailed.
keywords: Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs
Division of Occupied Areas Economic Affairs
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.5035, covering May 1946 to March 1948) concerns U.S. policy regarding Japanese combines (zaibatsu) and combinations in restraint of trade during the Allied occupation of Japan. The documentation consists of correspondence and internal routing slips involving the Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs and its successor, the Division of Occupied Areas Economic Affairs. Early records include the transmission of the three-volume Report of the Mission on Japanese Combines to Federal District Judge Pierson Hall following his work on Edwin Pauley's reparations mission, while later 1948 records address an external inquiry by attorney Eugene Sharp Bibb seeking a copy of Far Eastern Commission policy document FEC-230, which the State Department declined to release publicly while still under active multilateral consideration.

subfiles.about: Transmittal of the three-volume Report of the Mission on Japanese Combines to Federal District Court Judge Pierson Hall.
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman, Acting Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs
subfiles.summary: Roswell H. Whitman, Acting Chief of the Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, writes to Judge Pierson Hall of the Federal District Court in Los Angeles. Whitman acknowledges Hall's work on Edwin Pauley's final reparations report and his interest in Japanese combines. The letter confirms that a three-volume set of the Report of the Mission on Japanese Combines is being forwarded to Judge Hall under separate cover.
subfiles.title: Letter from Roswell H. Whitman to Judge Pierson Hall
subfiles.to: The Honorable Pierson Hall, Federal District Court, Los Angeles

subfiles.about: Internal State Department reference slip requesting identification and location of Far Eastern Commission document FEC-230.
subfiles.summary: A Department of State reference slip from Henke addressed to the Office of Far Eastern Affairs (FE) asking to identify the report designated as FEC-230. The sender requests that the document, if available, be forwarded to Room 306 - 3A-5 - PB. This inter-office inquiry was initiated to handle an incoming public request for the report.
subfiles.title: Reference Slip from Henke to Office of Far Eastern Affairs regarding FEC-230

subfiles.about: Inquiry and request from an attorney to the Department of State seeking a copy of document FEC-230.
subfiles.from: Eugene Sharp Bibb, Counsellor at Law
subfiles.summary: New York attorney Eugene Sharp Bibb writes to the Department of State requesting a copy of FEC-230, which he describes as a Far Eastern Commission recommendation regarding business policies in Japan. Bibb offers to promptly remit any expenses necessary to obtain the document. A notation on the letter indicates that a reply was assigned to H. Devere for drafting on March 2, 1948.
subfiles.title: Letter from Eugene Sharp Bibb to the Department of State requesting FEC-230
subfiles.to: Department of State, Washington, D. C.

subfiles.about: Official response declining to provide a copy of FEC-230 because the anti-trust policy document was still under active consideration by the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman, Acting Chief, Division of Occupied Areas Economic Affairs
subfiles.summary: Roswell H. Whitman, Acting Chief of the Division of Occupied Areas Economic Affairs, replies to Eugene Sharp Bibb's inquiry regarding document FEC-230. Whitman clarifies that FEC-230 relates specifically to anti-trust policy in Japan rather than overall economic policy, and explains that it remains under active consideration by the Far Eastern Commission. Consequently, it cannot be made public at this time, though Whitman assures Bibb that a copy will be sent promptly once an approved policy is released.
subfiles.title: Letter from Roswell H. Whitman to Eugene Sharp Bibb regarding FEC-230
subfiles.to: Eugene Sharp Bibb, Counsellor at Law
